clue.text: Old men perhaps foil security measure

parts.note: an old man is slang for a father, so old men are pas, the 'perhaps' marking it as one reading
a foil is a light fencing sword

explanation.surface: A security guard foils an attack, with pensioners as the threat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old man' is informal for father, so 'Old men perhaps' gives PAS, fathers.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret word typed or spoken to gain entry is a standard security measure.

clue.text: First of advance military units reach river on the Russian-Chinese border

indicators.note: taken to apply to each of the following four words, so their opening letters are taken in turn

explanation.surface: Forward troops arrive at a frontier river in the Far East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First of' reads as applying only to 'advance', but it takes the opening letter of each of the next four words.
explanation.definitionFit: The Amur is the long Asian river forming much of the frontier between Russia and China.

clue.text: Against poetry being recited

indicators.note: recited means spoken out, so the word for poetry is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: poetry is made of lines called verses

explanation.surface: Someone is opposed to poems being read out.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin-derived preposition used in sport and law means opposed to, as in one team against another.

clue.text: Wrong to assume husband butts in here

indicators.note: assume means take on, so the word for wrong takes in the husband letter

parts.note: to go wrong is to go astray

explanation.surface: A husband interrupts, wrongly presuming things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butts in' looks like interrupting, but the butts are cigarette ends stubbed out in the receptacle.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish for stubbing out cigarettes is where the ends or butts are put.

clue.text: Most inactive and poorly during Second International

indicators.note: during means within the time of, so the word for poorly goes inside the following letters

parts.note: an international cricket match is a Test
poorly means ill

explanation.surface: A sportsman is barely moving, being unwell during a second international match.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is an international match in cricket or rugby.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of still, meaning motionless, so the most motionless or inactive.

clue.text: Help idiot start to improve posture

parts.note: an ass is a fool

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: a stance is a way of standing, a posture

explanation.surface: Advice to a fool: begin by standing up straight.
explanation.definitionFit: Assistance and help are plain synonyms, both meaning aid given to someone.

clue.text: Lower status of French ace

parts.note: de is French for of
ace and mean are both slang for excellent, as in a mean guitarist

explanation.surface: A French ace pilot loses rank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mean' in slang praises skill, as in 'plays a mean guitar'.
explanation.definitionFit: To demean someone is to degrade them, lowering their dignity or standing.

clue.text: Unflappability of working-class men

indicators.note: working means being processed, so the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Praise for the composure of labouring men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working-class' reads as one compound adjective, but 'working' is the anagram signal on CLASSMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unflappable means staying composed and unruffled, which is a synonym of serenity.

clue.text: Sense of time wasted knowing no bounds

indicators.note: a word with no bounds has lost its outer letters, so only its inside remains

explanation.surface: Someone's sense of time is lost and limitless.
explanation.definitionFit: Taste is one of the five senses, the one exercised by the tongue.

clue.text: One exploits setters about to retire

parts.note: the setter is 'me', so several setters are 'us'

indicators.note: to retire is to go back, so the word for about is turned round

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone takes advantage of puzzle setters on the verge of retirement.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords the setter refers to themselves as ME, so plural setters are US.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who uses a person or thing can be one who exploits them for gain.

clue.text: Met privileged groups carrying large revolvers

parts.note: a committee that met sat

indicators.note: carrying means holding, so the groups contain the large letter

parts.note: elites are privileged groups in society

explanation.surface: The Metropolitan Police meet privileged gangs armed with big handguns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Met' suggests the London police and 'revolvers' guns; here they mean sat and orbiting bodies.
explanation.definitionFit: Moons and spacecraft revolve around planets, so they are things that revolve in orbit.

clue.text: Lots of powerless lackeys

indicators.note: powerless means without power, so the letter for power is dropped

parts.note: a poodle is a servile follower, a lackey

explanation.surface: Many hangers-on without any power.
explanation.walkthrough: P is the abbreviation for power.
explanation.definitionFit: Oodles is informal for a great quantity, so it means lots.

clue.text: When all else fails, option Carry On Cleethorpes?

parts.note: to carry on is to last, keep going
Cleethorpes is an example of a seaside resort, the question mark marking an example

explanation.surface: A desperate film idea: a Carry On comedy set in Cleethorpes.
explanation.walkthrough: Carry On films are a long British comedy series; Cleethorpes is a seaside resort on England's Lincolnshire coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names the final course of action, used only once every other option has failed.

clue.text: Warning triangle is broken

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so the letters are put back in another order

explanation.surface: A driver is told the roadside warning triangle is damaged.
explanation.definitionFit: Alerting someone means warning them, both being participles of verbs of caution.

clue.text: Part of somebody's Seychelles journey

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone's holiday trip to the Seychelles, in part.
explanation.definitionFit: Named after Homer's tale of Odysseus, the word means any long, eventful journey.

clue.text: Gets excited over detailed porcelain plates

indicators.note: over here means covering, so the scrambled letters go around the porcelain
excited means stirred up, so these letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: detailed means with the tail cut off, so the last letter goes

parts.note: china is porcelain

explanation.surface: Someone gets worked up about intricate porcelain plates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plates' reads as dinnerware beside 'porcelain', but here it means printed pictures; 'excited' makes ETGS, wrapped round the cut-short china.
explanation.definitionFit: Etchings are prints made from engraved metal plates, and plates is a printer's term for such prints.

clue.text: Briefly anointed barbarous Boris Johnson?

indicators.note: barbarous means wild and savage, so the letters are wildly rearranged
briefly means cut short, so the last letter of the word goes

explanation.surface: A former Prime Minister crudely given a quick blessing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' drops the D from ANOINTED, and 'barbarous' rearranges ANOINTE; Boris Johnson went to Eton, the English public school.
explanation.definitionFit: Boris Johnson was educated at Eton College, so he is an example of a former pupil; the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: Bitterness of American crook, regularly missing bounty

parts.note: crim is informal for criminal, a crook

indicators.note: letters missing at regular intervals leave every other one

explanation.surface: An American criminal is bitter at missing out on the reward.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrimony is harsh, bitter feeling, especially in a dispute, so a synonym of rancour.

clue.text: Content to leave alcohol, rising QC consumes a lime and soda?

indicators.note: the content of a word is its inside, so when it leaves only the outer letters stay
consumes means swallows, so the reversed word takes the article inside
in a down entry rising means read upwards, so the word is turned round

parts.note: a Queen's Counsel is a senior barrister who 'takes silk'

explanation.surface: A lawyer gives up drink and orders a lime and soda.
explanation.walkthrough: QC is a senior British barrister, known as a silk; 'rising' reverses SILK to KLIS, which takes in A.
explanation.definitionFit: Lime and soda are both chemical bases; the question mark warns they are examples, not the drink.

clue.text: Male rewriting article using feet

indicators.note: rewriting means setting down again differently, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man redrafts an essay with his feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Verse is measured in metrical feet, units of stressed and unstressed syllables, so metrical writing uses them.

clue.text: Selfishness perhaps is in order

parts.note: e.g. means for example, standing for perhaps

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the word is goes within the order

parts.note: the OM is the Order of Merit

explanation.surface: A tidy claim that selfishness may be appropriate.
explanation.walkthrough: The OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Egoism is the habit of putting oneself first, which is a synonym of self-centredness.

clue.text: French revolutionary losing clothes in US capital

indicators.note: losing means giving up, so the clothes are taken from the revolutionary

parts.note: Robespierre was a leader of the French Revolution
robes are clothes

explanation.surface: A French revolutionary strips off in Washington.
explanation.walkthrough: 'US capital' suggests Washington, but it is a state capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierre is the capital city of the US state of South Dakota.

clue.text: Tipsy Chechens, full of spirit

indicators.note: these words are full of the answer, which sits inside them across the word break

explanation.surface: Drunken Chechens have had plenty of spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirit' suggests strong drink beside 'Tipsy', but it means the soul.
explanation.definitionFit: The psyche is the human soul or mind, an older sense of the spirit within.

clue.text: Tory's buccaneering plot

parts.note: a Conservative is a Con, so Tory's gives Con's
buccaneering is piracy at sea

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician's swashbuckling scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: Con is short for Conservative, the UK party whose members are called Tories.
explanation.definitionFit: A conspiracy is a secret plan by a group, so a synonym of a scheme or intrigue.

clue.text: Dull sound of rubbish piano

parts.note: bum is slang for worthless, rubbish
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A poor piano gives a dull note.
explanation.definitionFit: A bump is the dull thud of something heavy hitting a surface.

clue.text: Girls losing useful devices in coach seats

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the remainder goes within the coach

parts.note: a coach is a bus

indicators.note: losing means doing without, so the devices are taken from the girls

parts.note: maids are girls
aids are useful devices, as in hearing aids

explanation.surface: Girls lose their gadgets on the coach seats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seats' suggests the coach's chairs, but it is a polite word for what sits on them; 'losing' leaves the single letter M.
explanation.definitionFit: Seat is a polite word for the buttocks, and bums is the British slang for them.

clue.text: Little growth in season once November's gone

indicators.note: N is the radio alphabet's November, and once it is gone the letter is removed

parts.note: spring is a season

explanation.surface: Some small new shoots appear in a season after November.
explanation.walkthrough: November is N in the NATO phonetic alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprig is a small shoot or twig, a little bit of plant growth.

clue.text: Stupid bears smell beastly

indicators.note: bears means carries, so the word for stupid holds the smell

parts.note: inane means stupid
hum is British slang for a bad smell

explanation.surface: Silly bears give off a horrible stink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bears' looks like animals, matching 'beastly', but it is the verb carry.
explanation.definitionFit: Inhumane means cruel, lacking compassion, which is what beastly means of behaviour.
